articles.title: Jensen Huang says he would be ‘honored’ to return as Nvidia’s CEO if he were asked
articles.summary: Jensen Huang said Tuesday that he would be “honored” to return to his job as CEO of Nvidia if the chip giant’s board of directors decided to bring him back.
articles.body: Jensen Huang said Tuesday that he would be “honored” to return to his job as CEO of Nvidia if the chip giant’s board of directors decided to bring him back. In a statement posted to X, Huang, who resigned as CEO last week over allegations of extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, said he would welcome the opportunity to retake the reins of the company he co-founded in 1993. “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said in a short statement. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.” Huang also said he “did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life.” “I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret,” he said. “I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.” A portion of the statement was first reported by The Wall Street Journal, prompting shares of Nvidia to erase their earlier losses. Earlier Tuesday, Republicans announced that Huang had agreed to sit for an interview with several House committees about whether the computer chip giant’s sales to China may have endangered U.S. national security. Huang is set to appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and the House Intelligence Committee on Dec. 1. Nvidia’s general counsel Tim Teter will sit for an interview the following day. Their remarks will not be publicly televised but will be transcribed and could be released at a later date. “We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security,” the chairmen of the three committees — Republican Reps. Brian Mast of Florida, John Moolenaar of Michigan and Rick Crawford of Arkansas — said in a joint statement Tuesday. “The American people need answers on Mr. Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous PRC actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal,” they wrote referring to the People’s Republic of China. Nvidia has previously denied violating any national security laws and said that it makes every effort to comply with protocols for overseas sales. “We look forward to meeting with the Chairmen on December 2,” an Nvidia spokesperson said in an email, notably referring only to the date of Teter’s interview, and not Huang’s. Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO last week following allegations of extramarital relationships, including one with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. The company is expected to report quarterly earnings following the market close Tuesday. Analysts will be closely watching Nvidia’s outlook for future chip sales, and whether slowdowns elsewhere in the AI space are impacting the company. Nvidia shares have declined more than 13% over the past week and 28% over the past month, as a confluence of factors have spooked investors, including higher costs, Democratic midterm election victories and cracks in AI demand that have helped send tech stocks broadly lower. “Nvidia’s stock is not just falling because of the loss of Jensen and the China scrutiny,” said said Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at OnePoint BFG financial group. “At the end of the day, they are also another picks and shovels company selling their wares into the data center buildout and we’ve seen what’s happened to many of those stocks, they are down sharply,” he wrote in a note early Tuesday.

articles.title: JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum to step down as Jamie Dimon's succession plans take shape
articles.summary: JPMorgan Chase said Tuesday that longtime chief financial officer Jeremy Barnum will step down next year in the latest change among the top ranks of the coun...
articles.body:
JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) said Tuesday that longtime CFO Jeremy Barnum will step down next year in the latest change among the top ranks of the country's largest bank as it prepares for CEO Jamie Dimon's eventual succession.

Barnum, who has served as the bank's CFO since 2021, will be succeeded by Bregje de Best, CFO of JPMorgan's commercial and investment bank, after the company's first quarter earnings in April, according to a JPMorgan filing .

Barnum will become vice chair, remaining with the bank until early 2028, JPMorgan said. Dimon added in a press release statement that Barnum had requested the transition after six years in the role.

That tenure is slightly above average for a CFO at a large US company, according to a 2025 study by executive search firm Spencer Stuart, which found CFOs at S&P 500 companies had served an average of 4.8 years in their positions.

The announcement comes less than a week after Allison Beer, JPMorgan's head of credit card and connected commerce, informed colleagues that she was leaving to pursue another opportunity, according to an internal JPMorgan memo.

It also follows a broader leadership shake-up of Dimon's top lieutenants earlier this year when JPMorgan announced the retirement of Marianne Lake, the former head of its sprawling consumer bank and previously a leading candidate to succeed Dimon .

The announcement of Lake's departure also came as JPMorgan said it was elevating executives Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh to the role of co-president, signaling their leads to eventually take the reins from Dimon, who was expected to stay for three more years as CEO, according to an executive familiar with the matter who spoke to Yahoo Finance at the time.

Barnum's planned transition and Lake's retirement are part of a broader effort to prepare JPMorgan's next generation of leadership, according to a person familiar with the bank's succession planning.

The person characterized Beer's departure as separate, saying the credit card executive was seeking a broader leadership role than her current responsibilities at the bank.

De Best, 43, joined JPMorgan in 2006 and has held senior positions across investment banking, markets and corporate banking. She will also join the firm's operating committee when she assumes the CFO role.

Morgan Stanley analyst Manan Gosalia said Tuesday his team "do[es] not expect the CFO transition itself to have any impact on JPM's strategy or preliminary 2027 outlook."

RBC Capital Markets analyst Gerard Cassidy also told clients Tuesday, in reaction to Barnum's departure, that senior management shake-ups are not unusual at JPMorgan.

"We expect JPM's deep management bench will continue to enable the company to effectively manage through senior executive realignment," Cassidy said.

articles.title: Kalshi moves into a new kind of gambling: the stock market
articles.summary: Kalshi is getting ready to launch stock trading on its platform, according to a report from The Wall Street Journal.
articles.body: Kalshi is getting ready to offer stock trading on its platform, according to reports from The Wall Street Journal and CNBC. The company reportedly plans to use its acquisition of broker FB Securities to launch equities and exchange-traded funds “within the next two months,” pitting the prediction market against rivals like Robinhood. The rumored expansion into stock trading comes as Kalshi faces a growing number of legal battles over its prediction market platform across the US. New York, Nevada, New Mexico, Washington, Connecticut, and several others have accused Kalshi of operating illegally in their states, while Utah recently filed criminal charges against Kalshi and its CEO. At the same time, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission is pushing back on state efforts to regulate prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket, arguing that it has the “exclusive” authority over them. Nine Democratic senators wrote a letter to the CFTC this week, urging it to stop interfering with state bans on prediction markets.

articles.title: New Bond sparks luxury brands battle for a place alongside 007
articles.summary: By Helen Reid LONDON, Nov 17 (Reuters) - James Bond has a new leading man, and luxury brands are already jockeying for a role alongside him. More than 60 yea...
articles.body:
LONDON, Nov 17 (Reuters) - James Bond has a new leading man, and luxury brands are already jockeying for a role alongside him.

More than 60 years after "Dr. No" introduced 007 to cinema audiences, Bond remains one of the world's most coveted marketing vehicles, with watchmakers, carmakers, fashion houses and drinks brands ‌spending millions around each film in the hope of being associated with Britain's best-known secret agent.

The naming of Robert Pattinson, 40, ends years of speculation over who ‌would inherit the role after the franchise killed off Daniel Craig's Bond in 2021's "No Time to Die". Craig wore Omega watches, drove Aston Martin cars and was dressed by Tom Ford.

Branding experts said the first Bond film under ​Amazon MGM Studios and director Denis Villeneuve offers a rare chance for luxury groups to reshape one of Hollywood's most closely watched product-placement portfolios.

"James Bond occupies a special place in terms of branding," said Eric Nebot, founder and CEO of product-placement agency Hill Valley, who worked with Swiss jeweller Chopard on "No Time to Die".

"He is an icon of cinema who has been created partly through the clothes he wears, the brands he uses and the cocktails he drinks."

The unveiling of Pattinson as Bond — with no watch on his wrist — set phones ablaze within Hollywood's product-placement industry. The actor appeals to ‌men and women across generations, from his early "Twilight" fanbase to "Batman".

"I ⁠love the Pattinson choice. It gives us a lot to work with," said Britt Johnson, CEO and founder of Mediaplacement, an agency that placed Diageo's Smirnoff vodka in Bond's trademark martini in the 2021 film.

"For Bond, having a female audience is very, very important," he added, pointing to Pattinson's ⁠standing in the fashion world.

Pattinson has been an ambassador for LVMH's Dior for more than a decade and in September became a global face of luxury Swiss watch brand Jaeger-LeCoultre, owned by Richemont.

Pattinson's deal with Jaeger-LeCoultre could create tensions with Swatch-owned Omega, Bond's official watch brand since Pierce Brosnan wore one in 1995's "GoldenEye". Earlier movies, as well as Ian Fleming's original novels, associated Bond with Rolex.

"The watch category will ​likely ​be the biggest conflict to resolve," said Anne Biskin, co-founder of SMG Entertainment in Portland, Oregon. She added ​that brands involved in previous Bond films could have a right of ‌first refusal to return.

Omega declined to comment. Jaeger-LeCoultre did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Amazon MGM said it was too early to comment on possible brand partnerships.

articles.title: US authorities interviewed Alice Huang in probe over possible diversion of chips
articles.summary: The US Commerce and Justice Departments revealed that detail in a joint statement, following days of mounting scrutiny of US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.
articles.body: US investigators conducted an in-person interview with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang last summer, the US Commerce and Justice Departments said, as part of an investigation into whether the Singapore-based company had been diverting highly coveted US semiconductors. The departments included that detail in a joint statement released late Monday, which laid out a timeline of their investigation into the cloud computing and data center provider. The Commerce Department launched an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations, the departments said. The statement comes after days of mounting scrutiny of US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who has faced criticism for being too slow in taking action against Megaspeed. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent added to the pressure on Friday, accusing the Commerce Department of a delay in labeling the Nvidia customer a possible national security threat. The departments said Commerce investigators requested records in May 2025 from Nvidia concerning “direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed,” and that Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its “no sell” list the following month. Following that, agents from agents from the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, in conjunction with Singaporean law enforcement officials, “conducted an on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed in June 2025 and interviewed CEO Alice Huang,” the joint statement said. US government officials have identified Alice Huang as having had an affair with then-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and have raised concerns that she could be a potential Chinese intelligence asset. The US intelligence community has been working to understand the relationship between Alice Huang and the Chinese government, with multiple sources telling CNN that the intelligence collected on her to date does not prove that she was acting as a spy for Beijing. Megaspeed said in a statement Sunday that Alice Huang left the company in August 2025 and currently holds no role there. It also said that the company is “aware of recent media reports containing assertions about our business, supply chain and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence.” Megaspeed did not immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday. Monday’s statement offered few other details, but said that the Justice Department has since taken on the lead role in the criminal investigation into Megaspeed. “The Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security working together will bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred,” it said. The statement follows similar details released last week by the Singaporean government, which also noted US authorities’ visit to Megaspeed last summer. It said the Bureau of Industry and Security conducted a check at Megaspeed, “with Huang present,” on June 24, 2025, which “was the first time Singapore came to know about the US’s interest in Megaspeed and Huang,” the Ministry of Home Affairs said in a statement. That same day, Singaporean police also interviewed her as part of its ongoing investigations into Megaspeed, and her passport was impounded to secure her attendance for purposes of the ongoing investigations, since Alice Huang was not based in Singapore, the statement said. Ultimately, the Singapore Police Force concluded there was “insufficient evidence” that Alice Huang had committed any offenses relating to the investigation, but she was barred from re-entering the country due to attempts to “downplay her role” at Megaspeed, the government said.

articles.title: Jensen Huang says he would be ‘honored’ to be reinstated as Nvidia CEO in new statement
articles.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who abruptly stepped down last week after a scandal involving extramarital affairs, said Tuesday he would be “honored” to return to the role if the board were to allow it.
articles.body: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who abruptly stepped down last week after a scandal involving extramarital affairs, said Tuesday he would be “honored” to return to the role if the board were to allow it. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret,” Huang said in a statement. He stepped down last week from the company he co-founded 33 years ago, ending an extraordinary run at the helm of one of the world’s most valuable companies. The resignation came just four days after the company’s board announced it was investigating him, following reports that he had multiple affairs, including one with Alice Huang, who sources have identified as a potential Chinese intelligence asset; as well as reports of another affair with an Nvidia executive. CNN’s numerous attempts to reach Alice Huang for comment have been unsuccessful. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Jensen Huang said in the statement, noting support he’s received. CNN has reached out to Nvidia for comment on Huang’s statement. The company’s board of directors, however, is not considering reinstating Huang, a source familiar with the situation told CNN. President Donald Trump, who frequently looked to Huang for guidance on the nation’s AI policies, said Monday he “would not mind” if Huang returned as CEO. Trump is scheduled to meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping later in the week. The president said he “may” discuss Nvidia with Xi. Beyond Trump, Huang has seen a strong showing of support in recent days – both from current and former Nvidia employees and across Silicon Valley. Elon Musk said in a post on X that he would be “honored” to hire Huang. The Tesla and SpaceX CEO also said he would be signing a growing petition for Nvidia’s board to bring back Huang. Big questions loom. Answers could soon come The US intelligence community is still working to understand the relationship between Alice Huang and the Chinese government. Multiple sources have told CNN that the intelligence collected on her to date does not prove that she was acting as a spy for Beijing. Nvidia is synonymous with the global AI boom, supplying some of the most advanced chips that power AI models for some of the world’s largest technology companies. On Thursday, Nvidia announced its Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as the company’s interim CEO while the board considers internal and external candidates. Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress in a hearing scheduled for December 1, and Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, will testify the following day. Both will be closed-door hearings with transcribed interviews subsequently released to the public. Huang previously apologized to his family and Nvidia employees in a company message last week, acknowledging that he had been unfaithful to his wife and saying he would cooperate with an independent investigation initiated by the company’s board of directors. “I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security,” he said last week. Alice Huang is a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based tech company and Nvidia customer. Some US sources say that whether or not she was recruited by China’s intelligence service, she posed a counterintelligence risk because Chinese national security law requires its citizens to assist in intelligence-gathering efforts if asked. Concerns have been mounting that chips Megaspeed purchased were diverted to Chinese entities, potentially skirting US export restrictions. Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing, saying it is a “compliant and legal company” and that it will cooperate with the US investigation. In a statement to CNN, Nvidia said allegations of illegal chip diversion were “thoroughly investigated and debunked last year.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the allegations that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy “groundless speculation and an attempt to smear and malign China.” Nvidia is scheduled to report its third-quarter earnings later on Tuesday and hold a subsequent call with analysts, which will be the first opportunity for the public to hear directly from the company’s new leadership.

articles.title: "Siendo mujer, aparte de ganar parece que tienes que ser perfecta"
articles.standfirst: Loida Zabala, Desi Vila y Lucía Martín-Portugués, que representan la nueva era del deporte femenino como referentes y como protagonistas, pasaron por el Business Sport Forum
articles.summary: Loida Zabala, Desi Vila y Lucía Martín-Portugués, que representan la nueva era del deporte femenino como referentes y como protagonistas, pasaron por el Business Sport Forum
articles.body: Tres deportistas de lujo para una mesa sobre la nueva era del deporte femenino español. Loida Zabala, deportista paralímpica de halterofilia; Desi Vila, atleta paralímpica y exgimnasta; y Lucía Martín-Portugués, esgrimista olímpica, especialista en sable y campeona de Europa este mismo año. Son referentes y fueron protagonistas en el Business Sport Forum, moderadas por Almudena Rivera, de MARCA, y siempre con el compromiso y la apuesta de Iberdrola como fondo. Loida, que más allá de sus méritos deportivos lucha contra el cáncer desde 2023, aludió a los primeros años de su carrera: "En 2008 empecé a seguir a la campeona mexicana, gran persona además, que incluso me invitó a su casa, pero al principio no tenía referencias. Aprendí a ser yo misma, siendo mi entrenamiento de cada semana mejor que el de la anterior". El tratamiento oncológico, por cierto, no evita que esté en su mejor momento: "Antes del diagnóstico no podía levantar más de 100 kilos y ahora intento los 110. Quiero llegar viva a 2028, para estar en los Juegos". Desi es gallega y quería ser como Ana Peleteiro. Pero también topó con limitaciones: "Las prótesis no las cubre la Seguridad Social [de hecho está creando una asociación para que los niños tengan acceso a ellas], las instalaciones no están adaptadas... Intentábamos analizar la biomecánica de mis rivales viendo videos. El mensaje, llegando al final de mi carrera deportiva, es que se puede hacer deporte adaptado y llegar a cumplir sueños como ir a los Juegos. Pero además de soñar se necesitan recursos". Lucía mejora con los años, "como el buen vino", apuntó Almudena. "El sable femenino comenzó este siglo a ser olímpico", explicaba Martín-Portugués. "Tuve la fortuna de coincidir con Coral Bistuer, siendo yo pequeña, y ella me abrió un mundo, el de mujeres integradas en el deporte. También me he dormido viendo muchísimos videos de Almudena Cid, que no se retiraba y seguía ganando. Yo he querido demostrar también que puedes visualizar en otras personas cosas que quieres para ti. Llegué a quedar última en un campeonato de Europa... y 13 años después fui campeona", añadió. Más allá de lamentar el acoso a través de las redes sociales, "mucho más acentuado para las mujeres que para los hombres", también se reivindicó la inclusión del deporte paralímpico en los Juegos Olímpicos, "como una categoría más y como deportistas que somos". Uno de los lemas manejados es muy claro, "insiste, resiste, persiste", y en eso andan las tres. Referentes. Protagonistas. "Siendo mujer, aparte de ganar parece que tienes que ser perfecta", dijo Lucía. "Si volviésemos a nacer, seríamos deportistas otra vez. Hacemos lo que nos gusta", coincidieron.

articles.title: Major fried chicken chain franchisee files Chapter 11 bankruptcy
articles.summary: The KFC and Taco Bell franchisee avoids sanctions that could have shut down its business.
articles.body:
Although consumer traffic at fried chicken restaurants increased by 3% in 2025, according to data firm Circana , certain major franchisees have continued to struggle with declining sales and rising costs.

Declining sales led a KFC and Taco Bell franchisee to file for bankruptcy to seek a sale of its assets.

Tasty Chick'n files Chapter 11 bankruptcy

Major KFC and KFC/Taco Bell co-branded franchisee Tasty Chick'n LLC filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, facing a potential termination of its franchise agreements over $15.6 million in unpaid royalties.

The Plano, Texas-based fried chicken dining chain franchisee and three affiliates filed their petition in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas, listing $50 million to $100 million in assets and $100 million to $500 million in liabilities, according to court papers.

Debtor counsel Jason S. Brookner of Gray Reed in Houston was not immediately available for comment.

Tasty Chick'n was formed in 2021 to develop, acquire, own, and operate KFC and Taco Bell branded restaurants through franchise agreements with KFC, Taco Bell, and parent Yum Brands, according to a declaration by Tasty Chick'n CEO Thomas M. Scott .

The franchisee is seeking a sale of its assets through the Chapter 11 bankruptcy case, the declaration said. It plans to market its restaurants as an entire portfolio, by individual market, or in combinations of different markets to maximize buyer participation and transaction value, court papers said.

The debtor will also seek $20 million in debtor-in-possession financing from prepetition lender MidCap Financial Trust, consisting of $5 million in new money and a $15 million rollup of prepetition debt.

The debtor owns and operates 75 KFC and 9 KFC/Taco Bell co-branded restaurants in 10 states, including Florida, Tennessee, Arkansas, Missouri, Mississippi, Alabama, Virginia, Kentucky, Illinois, and Indiana.

The fried chicken and taco fast-food franchisee asserted that revenue had declined significantly since the debtors acquired its restaurants, while food, labor, operating, and rent costs all increased, resulting in deteriorating restaurant-level EBITDA.

articles.title: From gases to machines, India builds its chip backbone
articles.summary: India’s semiconductor push shifts to execution: building supplier networks, training talent and boosting fab yields with AI, with firms like Tata and Applied Materials.
articles.body: Bengaluru: India’s semiconductor push is entering a phase in which reliable suppliers, specialised workers and better factory productivity will determine its global competitiveness, industry executives said at the Bengaluru Tech Summit on Tuesday.“We have moved from that ambition phase,” said Srinivas Satya, president of the components business and chief supply chain officer at Tata Electronics. “For us to be really competitive globally, we have to get the whole ecosystem to come together.”India’s projects span fabrication plants, which create chips on wafers, and packaging and testing units, which prepare them for use in devices. Tata is building a fab in Gujarat and a packaging plant in Assam; Micron, CG Semi and Kaynes are among the other packaging and testing players.Ashok Chandak, president of the India Electronics and Semiconductor Association and SEMI India, said Indian corporate investment was changing the industry’s prospects. “India’s manufacturing is not just dependent on government. Semiconductor manufacturing is now considered commercially, financially and strategically viable,” he said.Satya said Tata dealt with more than 1,200 suppliers across electronics and semiconductors, including over 500 in construction. “We have selected many small-scale engineering shops in the country, invited them into our factory and got them to develop solutions because we need that capability and responsiveness,” he said of its electronics operations. Tata would adapt that approach for semiconductors.The company is sending engineers to Taiwan for training and planning to use AI to improve factory productivity and yield — the proportion of usable chips produced.Applied Materials, which makes equipment used to manufacture chips, is seeking to expand its Bengaluru research facilities and India supplier base. “We need to grow our supply chain about 10 times,” said Radhika Viswanathan, COO of Applied Materials India.Its Bengaluru lab supports the development and testing of chipmaking equipment. “We are thinking about materials innovation, integrating these key innovations into our products and working with our customers to help ramp their yield,” she said.The dependencies extend to dozens of gases used to build layers on wafers, etch patterns and clean processing chambers. Diganta Sarma, head of strategy and business development at industrial and electronic gases supplier INOX Air Products, said semiconductor fabrication required about 50–60 gases.“It needs a lot of purification technology, analytics and redundancies to be built into the supply chain,” he said. That means checking purity and building backup arrangements for supplies. Gas producers and chipmakers must coordinate from the design stage, with production and delivery capacity ready as the factory ramps up.Sarma said the approach was to begin with gases needed in large volumes and partner with global companies that had the technology for others. Purity, supply reliability and the economics of producing each gas would shape that network. The objective, he said, was “to make sure that the fab never stops.”Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Supply chain gaps threaten India’s drone, space ambitions
articles.summary: India’s drone and spacetech startups warn supply chain gaps, import dependence and 52-week lead times could delay scaling and hurt global competitiveness.
articles.body: BENGALURU: India’s drone and spacetech startups face long procurement delays and dependence on imported components as they prepare to scale commercial operations, industry founders said at the Bengaluru Tech Summit on Tuesday.At a panel on India’s space economy, Denil Chawda, cofounder of GalaxEye, which builds Earth-observation satellites combining optical and radar imaging, said manufacturers remained dependent on imported semiconductors and integrated circuits. Supply disruptions could stretch project timelines from two years to five, costing companies valuable business opportunities.Lokesh Kabdal, co-founder of VyomIC, which is developing satellite-based precision navigation systems, said procurement lead times for some components extended to 52 weeks, making it difficult for Indian startups to compete globally. He also called for joint development programmes between ISRO and private companies, rather than treating startups primarily as vendors.Similar concerns emerged during a separate discussion on drone technologies.Parithi Govindaraju, founder of Uniko Aerospace, which develops long-endurance solar-powered drones for surveillance and industrial monitoring, said restrictions on sourcing components from China had narrowed procurement options, while India’s domestic ecosystem for specialised technologies remained underdeveloped.Vamshi Bharadwaj, founder of Yaanendriya, which develops precision sensors and navigation systems for drones and autonomous vehicles, said difficulties accessing high-precision components had pushed the company towards developing critical technologies in-house.Naman Pushp, founder of Airbound, which builds lightweight electric delivery drones, argued that indigenisation should go beyond manufacturing products domestically. “If we’re making it, I want us to make it better,” he said, emphasising globally competitive technology.Udi Hakim, CEO of Starbird AI, which develops GPS-independent navigation technology, said India offered an alternative manufacturing base for companies seeking China-free supply chains.Meanwhile, Abhijit Bhutey, cofounder of Inbound Aerospace, which develops reusable spacecraft to conduct research in orbit and return payloads to Earth, called for a dedicated spacecraft recovery range in India ahead of its planned 2028 mission.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says he'd be 'honored' to return to the company
articles.summary: Jensen Huang says he would be 'honored' to return as Nvidia CEO.
articles.body:
Former Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang says he would be "honored" to return as chief executive of the company he co-founded.

In a post on X Tuesday, Huang apologized to his family again and commented on the support he's seen among former employees, customers, and others seeking to have the company's board reinstate him.

A person familiar with the matter told Yahoo Finance that Nvidia's board is not looking to bring Huang back.

"Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," he wrote.

"Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."

Huang resigned late last week following revelations of multiple affairs, including one allegedly involving a suspected Chinese spy. Two other affairs were allegedly with Nvidia employees. This is his first public statement since the scandal erupted.

Nvidia has named CFO Colette Kress the company's interim CEO.

Huang's resignation has raised questions about whether Nvidia will continue its prodigious investments across the AI industry, how it will define its roadmap in the years ahead, and more.

The company has shed hundreds of billions of dollars in its market valuation since the scandals erupted.

Huang is now scheduled to appear before closed-door sessions of Congress on Dec. 1 to discuss his reported relationship with the alleged spy, Alice Huang.

The company is scheduled to report its Q3 earnings after the bell today.

articles.title: Disney holds the line on park pricing as screen-weary consumers seek 'real experiences'
articles.summary: Disney said it's on pace for more projects than ever before.
articles.body:
Disney doesn't plan to change its park pricing anytime soon, as its experiences segment, including both parks and cruises, hit a record revenue last quarter.

"We feel very good about the current trends," CEO Josh D'Amaro said, adding that bookings for the first quarter in 2027 are higher compared to 2026.

"It's more than about just ticket price," D'Amaro said. "Consumers want real experiences now … we're seeing that accelerate. People today are spending so much of their lives on screens. They're just looking for time to connect with each other in the real world … Disney parks [are] one of the few places that you can actually do that."

Disney saw a record number of guests at its parks last quarter, the company said. D'Amaro added that Disney has more projects underway around the world than "any other point in history."

A lot of Disney's focus is on its Orlando resort, especially on Monstropolis at Disney's Hollywood Studios, Lake Shore Lodge, and Tropical Americas in Animal Kingdom. Disney also has plans to double the size of the Avengers Campus at Disneyland California by 2028.

NerdWallet found that a seven-night trip to Disney with a family of four could easily top $6,000 — and that's for a "frugal traveler."

In the most recent quarter, Disney reported an 11% increase in global guests visiting its parks and experiences, led by Disneyland Paris. Disney also increased capacity for its Disney Cruise Line following the launches of the Disney Adventure and Disney Destiny cruise ships.

Customers spent more at Disney parks too. Average spending per customer on admissions, food, and merchandise in US parks rose 4%, more than the expected 3.6% in the US. Internationally, sales at Disneyland Paris offset weakness in Hong Kong and Shanghai parks.

While the company is largely holding firm on prices, it is offering promotions and programs for Florida residents, its annual passholders, and Disney+ subscribers.

Disney is also exploring offering a free ad-supported version of its Disney+ streaming service.

"We are exploring a free product, and I think it will be more price-sensitive consumer and bring in new Disney+ subscribers," D'Amaro told investors. "It's going to give us more ad inventory to … offer a key retention tool that, quite frankly, we currently don't have." A bundle deal for Disney+ and Hulu with ads currently costs $11.99 a month. Without ads, it costs $19.99 a month, and you're able to download movies and series. That could change soon.

articles.title: Groww Foundation, WELL Labs join hands to make Chintamani water-secure
articles.summary: Groww Foundation and WELL Labs launch a four-year plan with local authorities to make Chintamani water-secure via lake rejuvenation, recharge and supply upgrades.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Groww Foundation, the philanthropic arm of investment platform Groww, WELL Labs and local govt authorities have launched a four-year initiative to make Chintamani in Karnataka water-secure, with a focus on restoring lakes, augmenting drinking water sources and improving groundwater recharge.The programme, announced on Tuesday at an event titled ‘Securing Chintamani’s Water Futures’, will be implemented in collaboration with the Chintamani City Municipal Council and relevant govt authorities. The initiative also aims to develop a model that can be replicated in other small cities across South India.Chintamani, which depends heavily on groundwater and borewells, faces acute water shortages, particularly during summers. Municipal borewells are being drilled to depths of 1,000-1,600 feet but are struggling to meet the city’s growing water demand. During droughts, up to 70% of wells can run dry. The city also spends nearly 40% of its operational expenditure on running water supply infrastructure, with electricity costs continuing to rise.Under the initiative, the partners will rejuvenate degraded lakes by improving their water-holding capacity, preventing pollution and enhancing groundwater recharge. Where feasible, the restored lakes will also be developed as additional drinking water sources.The programme will also convert two public parks into ‘sponge parks’ to improve groundwater recharge, besides installing rooftop rainwater harvesting and recharge structures in public campuses. Water supply connectivity will be improved in two urban-poor communities, while WELL Labs will provide technical assistance to the municipal council on integrated urban water management.“At Groww Foundation, we have always looked at supporting initiatives that take an innovation-first lens to create meaningful impact in people’s lives,” said Kalpana Swaminathan, head of Groww Foundation.WELL Labs executive director Veena Srinivasan said groundwater was the dominant source of water supply for most small cities in South India, and the initiative would demonstrate how science and collective action could help address the challenge.WELL Labs has spent the past three years conducting research, field surveys and assessments in Chintamani, with research support from the UK and Canadian govts and CSR support from DCB Bank.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Social media algorithms are encouraging Americans to freak out about the tech outages
articles.summary: How do seemingly ordinary tech snafus become ominous signs of impending societal collapse? When they’re filtered through algorithms that reward alarmism, that’s how.
articles.body: How do seemingly ordinary tech snafus become ominous signs of impending societal collapse? When they’re filtered through algorithms that reward alarmism, that’s how. There’s a lot of that happening right now. Conspiracy theories about government plots and power blackouts are cropping up after the Microsoft cloud outage, the nationwide ground stop and other recent disruptions. My advice is simple: Don’t let the algorithms scare you. Preparedness is smart; panic is not. So let’s try to separate what’s real from what’s reckless. What’s real: The palpable and understandable anxiety right now about a succession of tech outages. “It has been one massive tech disruption after another, and it’s putting people on edge,” Kate Bolduan said on “CNN News Central.” People are asking if rogue AI systems, human hackers or other culprits are poking holes in the infrastructure we all take for granted. And government officials aren’t exactly assuaging the fears. “It’s fine,” President Donald Trump said glibly in response to a question about the outages on Tuesday. Widespread distrust in Trump, his administration and other institutions makes it harder to convince people that there’s nothing more sinister going on. But here’s the thing: Legit questions about the digital infrastructure underpinning our lives are being exploited by doomsday preppers and bad-faith actors. There are reckless comments all across Facebook and X, and conspiratorial videos all over TikTok and Instagram, that simply don’t reflect reality. No, there wasn’t a system outage at Costco on Monday. No, there wasn’t a secret test of the electrical grid. Yes, there was a test of the Emergency Alert System, but it was totally routine and maybe just poorly timed. Human brains are wired to look for patterns, and the endless scroll provides endless chances to find them, especially when social media influencers appear to be “just asking questions” about what’s going on. It’s wiser to seek out sources with actual answers, rather than just questions, and to look out the window after looking down at the phone. But let’s face it: Some people like to indulge in nightmare-scenario planning for the same reasons they enjoy disaster movies. More than one Fox News host on Monday night sounded like a full-blown prepper. The commentary is its own fuel, causing all sorts of conspiracy thinking, including from prominent political figures. Trump confidant Laura Loomer posted tweets on Monday saying “Doesn’t everything just feel so weird?” and telling her followers to “go get cash.” Other influencers have tried to connect dots that have no known connections — insinuating that a shadowy entity is laying the groundwork for something apocalyptic. Conspiracy mongers like Alex Jones have been making a living by peddling these storylines for years, surely hoping that viewers will never notice that the predicted doomsday has never arrived. So when these posts pop up in your feed, ask yourself: What could be motivating the poster? Are they trying to get me to reply (and give their account more attention) or buy something or advance a political agenda? Are they raking in affiliate fee revenue when they tell me to purchase emergency supplies, you know, just in case? There’s a reason why it’s called “doomscrolling.” Once your favorite social media platform knows you’re paying attention to a particular topic, it delivers more and more, often distorting how significant it really is. We each exist in a personalized media bubble. And in my bubble, at least, posters are passing the time comparing their emergency stockpiles and cracking jokes about what they’ll do if the lights go out. My response: I’m going to put down the phone and hang up some Christmas lights. Keeping it in perspective I don’t mean to be dismissive. It’s fair to wonder whether autonomous AI agents — and the IT pros trying to counter those rogue bots — are responsible for all this tech turbulence. And it’s logical to expect further trouble, Chris Krebs, the former director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, said on CNN’s “The Situation Room.” “I believe it’s going to get better in the long run, but I would expect to see disruptions in some services over the next several months,” Krebs said. That’s partly because “we’re using AI to find vulnerabilities in software and systems, and we’re patching systems at a rate far beyond anything in the past.” But “any time you do a patch, any time you roll an update, it can destabilize the system,” Krebs told CNN’s Pamela Brown. While that’s going on, we have to keep a sense of perspective, in part because algorithms don’t. I noticed many X accounts on Monday wildly overstating United’s brief system outage, which affected only a small number of flights. Monday’s outage was “so pedestrian, it’d be a non-story if not for what’s happened the last four days,” Thrifty Traveler editor Kyle Potter wrote. Customer complaints about online banking outages might not have made news, either, if not for last week’s Microsoft and Workday cloud software outages. And FEMA probably wouldn’t have posted a tweet saying “we’ve heard a lot of rumors” about Tuesday’s Emergency Alert System test. This routine test had been scheduled for months (I checked), but it was already being incorporated into some of this week’s conspiracy theories. There are “no blackouts, no secret emergencies,” FEMA tweeted. “Just our legally mandated, routine test on TV and radio at approximately 2:20 PM ET.” Officials told CNN the test went smoothly. As for all the emergency preparedness chatter on social media, Krebs pointed out on NBC’s “Today” show that FEMA recommends having “food, water and other supplies to last for several days” in the event of an emergency. Being prepared in the digital age also means having physical, offline copies of important documents and account numbers. “It sounds prepperish, but it’s really not,” Krebs said. “It’s just kind of being an adult in modern society.” This story has been updated with additional details.

articles.title: Iraqi PM heads to Lebanon amid push to explore oil routes beyond Hormuz
articles.summary: Ali al-Zaidi’s talks expected to include proposed project linking Tripoli in Lebanon to Kirkuk-Baniyas pipeline.
articles.body:
Beirut, Lebanon – Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi is set to visit Lebanon on his latest regional visit aimed at boosting economic cooperation amid the fallout from the US-Israel war on Iran.

Al-Zaidi will hold a series of high-level meetings in Beirut, including with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam and Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri.

High on the agenda of Wednesday’s talks will be strengthening bilateral trade, customs exemption deals and coordination on security and countering drug trafficking.

Diversifying oil export routes via a pipeline linking the Iraqi city of Kirkuk, through Syria’s Mediterranean port of Baniyas, to Tripoli in northern Lebanon, is also expected to be discussed. The proposed project is aimed at potentially bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, a key energy waterway that has been severely disrupted since the start of the US-Israel war on Iran in late February.

“After the war in Iran and the story of Hormuz and exports in the Gulf, [Iraq] is looking for alternative routes to diversify their export routes,” Walid Marrouch, professor of economics at the Lebanese American University in Beirut, told Al Jazeera.

Iraq’s crude oil exports were badly hit following the start of the Iran war and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of the world’s energy passes in peacetime.

Last month, Iraq’s Ministry of Oil said crude oil exports reached about 2.7 million barrels per day (bpd), up from some 200,000 bpd in May. Before the war, Iraq was exporting about 3.5 million bpd. The increase has been boosted by the resumption of oil pumping this week through the Iraqi-Turkish pipeline at an initial capacity of 120,000 bpd.

Still, Iraq has been looking for alternatives to export its crude oil, primarily through Syria, which was previously difficult due to international sanctions under the leadership of longtime ruler Bashar al-Assad, who was toppled in late 2024.

Tamer Badawi, an associate fellow with the Royal United Services Institute, said al-Zaidi’s visit to Lebanon was likely to be informed by US envoy Tom Barrack’s “efforts to diversify Iraq’s oil export routes across the region, particularly through Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, Syria and Lebanon”.

He added: “The broader ambition is to develop alternative export corridors connecting Iraq’s oil infrastructure to regional networks.”

One of the potential proposed alternatives is Tripoli, in northern Lebanon.

The impoverished city has emerged as an option because of the long-defunct pipeline from Kirkuk and a local refinery that in 1940 filtered 21,000 bpd of crude oil from Iraq, according to the Lebanese Directorate General of Oil. The refinery shut down in 1992, shortly after the end of the 15-year Lebanese Civil War in 1990.

Industry insiders say Tripoli’s oil infrastructure has three legacy lines with a historical peak capacity of 900,000 bpd.

While it would need to be repaired and renovated, a report this year by the Basil Fuleihan Institute of Finance (BFIF), an autonomous agency under the tutelage of Lebanon’s Finance Ministry, said “the terminal infrastructure remains a goldmine of latent capacity” with a moderate flow scenario of 300,000 to 500,000 bpd that could gain Lebanon annual revenues in the region of $80m to $275m.

The revenues could be a boon to the Lebanese economy, which has been beset by a complex economic and banking crisis since 2019 that has seen its currency lose more than 90 percent of its value and the majority of its population living in poverty.

Al-Zaidi’s trip to Beirut comes weeks after he met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in Damascus. During the visit, the two countries signed a cooperation agreement to rehabilitate the pipeline running from Kirkuk to Baniyas, in a project to be carried out by US energy giant Chevron.

“Upon rehabilitation, this groundbreaking project will have an initial transport capacity of 2 million barrels per day of crude oil,” the US Department of State said in a statement at the time.

Experts said al-Zaidi’s visit on Wednesday was a big opportunity for Lebanon to ensure its place in a prospective tripartite agreement with Syria and Iraq – but warned that if Lebanese officials failed to act, the country could be left behind.

“Lebanon can benefit, but if Lebanon does not get a seat at the table, it [could be circumvented] because Iraq can already reach the sea from Syria,” said Marrouch.

Before reaching Tripoli, Iraqi crude oil would have to pass through some 250km (155 miles) of Syrian territory.

Syria also has its own ports in Tartous and Latakia, with a smaller port in Banias. According to BFIF, Syria is set up to handle about 350,000 to 500,000 bpd, between refineries at Banias and Homs, “a direct Mediterranean outlet that circumvents both the Suez Canal and the Strait of Hormuz”.

The flow of crude oil through Syria would also be a boost for the country, where domestic oil production is currently insufficient and energy costs have spurred protests . Syrian officials have also warned about attacks on the Homs refinery.

But experts believe including Lebanon in the deal could still be beneficial for all parties.

Tripoli’s deepwater quays allow it to handle larger vessels, reducing freight costs per barrel for Iraqi crude and making the oil competitive in European and North American markets, said the BFIF report, adding that Tripoli’s coastline is “naturally shielded from harsh southern winds and rough swells,” unlike in Banias in Syria.

“This makes the port accessible year-round, even during severe Mediterranean winter storms that frequently force the closure of offshore loading operations in Banias,” the report said.

articles.title: Consumer staples stocks benefiting from a powerful rotation as tech gets slammed
articles.summary: Tech stocks have truly fallen out of favor with investors.
articles.body:
Investors continue to find comfort in boring consumer staples stocks as growth expectations for the tech giants driving the AI boom come under closer scrutiny.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) tech sector's ( XLK ) forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is currently 17.2 times, its lowest level since 2020, according to data crunched by Duality Research. The S&P 500's consumer staples ( XLP ) sector forward P/E ratio of 24.2 times is at the highest level since 1999.

The S&P 500 consumer staples and tech sectors are up 18.7% and 12.7%, respectively, on the year.

"Is staples the actual bubble here? The sector's years to date gains are almost entirely attributable to multiple expansion," Duality Research noted.

Investors are rotating aggressively into consumer staples stocks to seek shelter from the sharp sell-off in high-flying technology and artificial intelligence shares.

Persistent inflation and elevated borrowing costs are squeezing household budgets, pushing shoppers to prioritize everyday necessities over discretionary upgrades.

Companies like Costco ( COST ), Procter & Gamble ( PG ), and Coca-Cola ( KO ) sell essential goods, and their cash flows and pricing power remain resilient during economic slowdowns. Additionally, these mature businesses offer reliable dividend yields that attract capital during periods of broader market volatility.

As institutional funds rebalance away from crowded momentum trades, staples have emerged as a safe-haven trade.

You can see it in the tape: P&G shares are up 9% over the past month, Coca-Cola is trading near a record high, and even struggling Campbell's ( CPB ) has seen its stock climb 20% in the past month.

Despite higher prices for consumer goods, consumers haven't retrenched — which has also helped sentiment on staples.

"The US consumer is remarkably resilient," P&G CFO Andre Schulten told Yahoo Finance in late October.

Schulten said the business is being powered by higher-income households, while the lower end is being more cautious.

articles.title: Arturo Guillén: "No tengo la menor duda de que las MMA van a ser el primer deporte del mundo"
articles.standfirst: El fundador de WOW FC reivindica el potencial de las artes marciales mixtas en una mesa en la que Víctor Claver, José Hidalgo y Rubén Martín analizaron los nuevos negocios y audiencias del deporte
articles.summary: El fundador de WOW FC reivindica el potencial de las artes marciales mixtas en una mesa en la que Víctor Claver, José Hidalgo y Rubén Martín analizaron los nuevos negocios y audiencias del deporte
articles.body: "No tengo la menor duda de que va a ser el primer deporte del mundo". Así de contundente se mostró Arturo Guillén, fundador y CEO de WOW FC, al hablar del futuro de las artes marciales mixtas (MMA), una disciplina que está experimentando un enorme crecimiento y que aspira a competir con los deportes más populares del planeta. Fue una de las reflexiones más destacadas de la mesa "Nuevos negocios del deporte: formatos, comunidades y audiencias", celebrada durante la IV edición del Expansión & MARCA Business Forum, que reunió también a Víctor Claver, exjugador de la NBA y cofundador de Players Hub 360; José Hidalgo, presidente de la Federación Española de Triatlón y de ADESP e impulsor de Hyatlon; y Rubén Martín, periodista deportivo y creador de contenido. Guillén, que llegó al mundo de las MMA después de más de tres décadas vinculado a la industria cinematográfica, explicó cómo pasó de analizar las taquillas de cine a convertirse en promotor de combates. "Si tú me hubieses preguntado hace unos años si me vería como promotor de combates, te habría dicho que es absolutamente imposible. Pero, en el fondo, el deporte y el entretenimiento es lo mismo. Competimos por la atención del consumidor", explicó. "No tengo la menor duda de que va a ser el primer deporte del mundo, porque es la esencia más primaria de la vida y del ser humano, que es la lucha. Bien tratado, bien enfocado, con los medios adecuados y bien contadas las historias de los peleadores, llega a una audiencia muy amplia", aseguró Guillén, que destacó cómo WOW está consiguiendo atraer a un público muy diverso. "La media de edad que tenemos es inferior a los 30 años y un montón de mujeres también. A veces ha estado en el 44% de mujeres". El empresario también explicó cómo llegó Cristiano Ronaldo a vincularse con WOW FC. "Fue algo muy orgánico. A través de un contacto le acercaron el tema de WOW y mostró interés. Le escribí una carta explicándole un poco cuál era la organización y me di cuenta de que los valores que proponemos como entidad deportiva son los que propone él: esfuerzo, compromiso, trabajo y excelencia. Enseguida nos dimos cuenta de que hablábamos de lo mismo". "Es una empresa audiovisual que cuenta historias, las historias de los peleadores. Tenemos peleadoras que son doctoras en biomedicina, tenemos ingenieros, taxistas, gente que ha estado en la cárcel... Gente que ha encontrado un camino de crecimiento personal a través de la lucha", explicó. En cuanto a la expansión audiovisual del proyecto, anunció un paso importante: "Ayer anunciamos que íbamos a estar en Disney+, lo cual nos llena de orgullo". Víctor Claver explicó cómo nació Players Hub 360, el proyecto que puso en marcha junto a otros deportistas tras retirarse en 2024. "Somos varios deportistas, la mayoría de básquet y fútbol, pero también hay alguno de triatlón y esperamos que pronto haya más, principalmente para crear proyectos que ayuden a otros deportistas", señaló el exjugador del Barcelona y de la NBA. "Durante tu carrera a veces hay un vacío de apoyo para el ahora y el después. La formación educativa, la formación financiera, es algo que los deportistas no tienen en el día a día muchas veces. Entonces, dar ese apoyo como deportista y como muchos de nosotros que ahora ya estamos retirados, que hemos vivido esa transición, pues ayudar a otros deportistas que lo están viviendo o que lo van a vivir", explicó Claver. Una de las principales apuestas del proyecto es facilitar la formación durante la carrera deportiva. "La idea es crear una plataforma, una formación para deportistas que se adapte a sus horarios, que si no pueden estar de manera presencial o en directo, aunque sea online, puedan ver la clase, la sesión o el webinar cuando puedan. Al final son pequeñas píldoras, es plantar la semilla", detalló. Y puso como ejemplo su experiencia en Estados Unidos: "En la NBA se trabaja mucho desde que llegas. Tienes un curso obligado que tienes que hacer y te hablan un poco de todo. Eso es algo que aquí en Europa no se está haciendo tanto". Claver también abordó el futuro del baloncesto europeo y la posible llegada de una competición impulsada por la NBA. "La Euroliga se ha consolidado como la competición por excelencia en el baloncesto europeo, pero la FIBA junto con la NBA ha visto que hay un margen de mejora", señaló. "Como jugador que he sido, espero que se unifique, porque creo que eso también al aficionado le ayudará. A veces hay demasiadas competiciones y eso hace perder el interés. Si se llega a un acuerdo, ya sea con la NBA, con FIBA, creo que será mejor para el baloncesto". Otro de los nuevos negocios deportivos que protagonizaron la mesa fue Hyatlon, el proyecto impulsado por la Federación Española de Triatlón para desarrollar las carreras híbridas. José Hidalgo explicó cómo surgió la oportunidad de incorporar una disciplina en plena expansión. "Es el deporte que en este momento en el mundo está creciendo de una forma increíble, exponencial. Decidimos que por qué no debíamos ser los primeros", recordó. "Lo que necesita el deporte es precisamente lo que pueden ofrecer las federaciones, que es legitimidad. Es lo que yo llamo la federalización: crear una estructura para que el deporte sea sostenible, regular normas y que sea transparente", defendió Hidalgo. "Hemos sido capaces de poner en marcha el primer circuito a nivel mundial de Hyatlon. Estamos en pleno proceso de nacimiento de un nuevo deporte", añadió. El presidente de la Federación Española de Triatlón destacó el potencial de crecimiento que supone entrar en un mercado mucho más amplio que el del triatlón tradicional. "Fijaros lo que ha supuesto para un deporte como el triatlón, que tiene aproximadamente unos 100.000 practicantes aficionados, entrar en un mundo y un ecosistema donde hay 12 millones de personas. La comunidad que corre y la comunidad que está en un gimnasio. Yo siempre digo que lo que ha pasado ahora es que le hemos puesto una meta". Y adelantó los planes para el próximo año: "Ya tenemos cerradas las ocho sedes para el año que viene. Ahora mismo tenemos como 16 capitales de este país que quieren organizarlo con la Federación porque entienden que les aporta una seguridad que antes no había". Hidalgo confirmó que el circuito comenzará en Sevilla en febrero, terminará en Zaragoza y también pasará por Madrid, además de otras cinco ciudades todavía pendientes de anunciar. Rubén Martín aportó la perspectiva de los nuevos creadores de contenido y explicó cómo la pandemia cambió su trayectoria profesional. "Lo bonito sería decir que lo preparé, lo pensé y había una estrategia, pero la realidad es que no. Como a la mayoría de creadores de contenido, nos explotó un poco en la cara con la pandemia", reconoció. El periodista recordó especialmente el momento en el que Ibai Llanos le invitó a narrar un torneo de FIFA. "Me di cuenta de que los jugadores a los que nosotros, MARCA o la COPE, nos cuesta acceder, se peleaban por estar en el torneo de Ibai. Tenía que decirle que no a jugadores del Madrid, del Atlético o del Barça porque había más de los que querían. Yo dije: aquí pasa algo. Veías transmisiones en directo con millones de personas de todo el mundo y había algún sitio al que no estábamos llegando". Martín defendió que los medios tradicionales deben aprovechar las oportunidades que ofrecen las nuevas plataformas en lugar de verlas como una amenaza. "Lo recibimos con miedo, con recelo, como la resistencia al cambio que implica cualquier cambio importante. Pensábamos: estos que vienen ahora de YouTube, Twitch o Instagram, ¿vienen a matarnos o a hacernos más grandes?", reflexionó. "No le vamos a poner puertas al campo. Tienes que sumarte a ello y tratar de obtener el máximo beneficio, llegar a gente a la que no puedes llegar con tus propios medios, ser valiente, ser disruptivo". "MARCA se leía en los sitios a los que llegaba el periódico hace 50 años, donde llegaba al quiosco o al bar. Ahora, con una web, estés en el sitio del mundo en el que estés, nosotros, que compartimos idioma, tenemos 500 millones de potenciales lectores. Yo solo le veo ventajas. El único miedo que podría existir es el miedo al cambio", añadió. Por último, explicó su decisión de abandonar X, antes Twitter, pese a contar con más de un millón y medio de seguidores en redes sociales. "Yo no trabajo para las redes sociales. Las redes sociales trabajan para mí. Si Twitter quiere que yo trabaje para ellos, que me paguen", afirmó. "El impacto a cualquier precio para mí no tiene sentido. El impacto que yo necesito en mis redes me lo da TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Twitch. No hay que estar en todos los lados todo el tiempo". Cuatro modelos de negocio distintos que dejaron una misma conclusión: el deporte ya no compite únicamente por los resultados, sino también por la atención de unas audiencias que consumen contenidos de formas cada vez más diferentes.

articles.title: Jensen Huang agrees to testify before US House, says can resume CEO role
articles.summary: Huang said he is ready to return as Nvidia CEO if the company’s board would like him back at the helm.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang, the former CEO of chipmaker Nvidia, has agreed to appear in transcribed interviews with several United States House committees on December 1, even as he has said he would be “honored” to resume his job if the company’s board would like him to.

On Tuesday, the House Foreign Affairs Committee announced the upcoming interviews, which will also include the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and the House Intelligence Committee.

The US tech giant’s General Counsel Tim Teter will appear before the same committees on December 2 . It was not immediately clear whether the men would attend in person or speak remotely.

“We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security,” Republican chairmen of the committees, Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford, said in a statement.

“The American people need answers on Mr Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous PRC [People’s Republic of China] actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal.”

Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s CEO on Thursday after reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, raised questions over exports of the company’s advanced AI chips to China.

The lawmakers first called on Huang on November 5 to appear before the committees. That came amid initial reports from The New York Times that US authorities had started investigating Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, which buys artificial intelligence (AI) chips from Nvidia, and with whom Huang has admitted to having an affair.

US authorities have scrutinised Megaspeed over suspicions that it helped Beijing gain access to advanced AI chips that are barred from shipment to China.

The announcement comes as Huang has expressed a willingness to return to the company since resigning last Thursday.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said in a post on the social media platform X.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

Huang’s comments come amid reports that tech industry insiders were pushing for his return to the company, alongside a petition with more than 177,000 people calling for his return.

“The board’s decision now sits between a founder who has publicly asked for his job back, a shareholder base with the means to force the question, and an administration split between a president open to his return and a Treasury secretary demanding an outsider,” Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives, said in a note provided to Al Jazeera.

At the same time, Nvidia has announced a board-level committee to oversee national security and export controls, marking the first major governance move since Huang resigned.

The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former Goldman Sachs vice chair, Nvidia said. Directors Stephen Neal, former CEO of law firm Cooley, and John Dabiri, a Caltech professor, will also serve on the committee.

US President Donald Trump welcomed the move, calling the launch of a national security initiative a good idea.

Nvidia stock tumbled in midday trading on Tuesday. It was down more than 1.6 percent for the day, 11 percent over the previous five days and 29.2 percent over the previous month.

articles.title: Unzué: "En el horizonte vamos a tener algún corredor español para pelear por las grandes vueltas"
articles.standfirst: El manager general del Movistar Team cerró la IV edición del Expansión & MARCA Business Sport Forum
articles.summary: El manager general del Movistar Team cerró la IV edición del Expansión & MARCA Business Sport Forum
articles.body: La IV edición del Expansión & MARCA Business Sport Forum se cerró con una charla de treinta minutos entre Eusebio Unzué, manager general de Movistar Team, y Nacho Labarga, redactor de MARCA. La conversación, bajo el título 'Construir un equipo que perdura: liderazgo, talento y patrocinio', giró en torno al éxito del Movistar Team en el pelotón internacional en los últimos 46 años, nada menos. Para empezar, Unzué recordó los inicios. "Cuando comenzamos, en el 74, el primer patrocinio con Reynolds y desde el 80 hasta hoy con los diferentes sponsors. Todo ha sido por tener unas estructuras muy válidas y la confianza de nuestros corredores. Eso ha hecho que lo más imprescindible, que es el patrocinio, hayamos podido ser atractivos. Por supuesto buscar resultado, pero por encima de todo, la satisfacción de todos los sponsors", señaló. Un mensaje, el de la satisfacción de los sponsors, que repitió durante toda la charla. Y es que, como apuntó Labarga, en el ciclismo no hay espectadores que paguen su entrada y todo el dinero tiene que ver con los patrocinadores. "En el año 80 cuando empezamos, nuestra primera Vuelta a España, nos costó el equivalente a 75.000 euros, no llegaba a 13 millones de pesetas. Y éramos casi 25 personas. Era un deporte muy latino, España, Francia, Bélgica y España. Hoy hablamos de equipos, en nuestra liga mundial, que prácticamente ninguno tiene menos de 20 millones y alguno por encima de los 50 ó 60 millones. Es la evolución de nuestro deporte. Y señala la globalización, de la que los medios habéis tenido una culpa muy importante, pero no cabe duda que la televisión fue determinante. Fue la que causó la repercusión en la que ahora nos encontramos. La televisión nos ayudó a que el ciclismo se comenzara a ver de otra manera. Fue la que nos llevó a entender que éramos el elemento ideal para promocionar las campañas de turismo. Terminar en los Campos Elíseos, en la Castellana o en lugares increíbles. Permite que la gente vaya conociendo diferentes sitios. Eso ha hecho que hoy comencemos en Australia y hayamos terminado hace un año en China". ¿Y para cuándo una mayor monetización de ese espectáculo televisivo? Unzué lo espera, pero no es optimista con que vaya a ser pronto. "Hay inquietudes, pero desgraciadamente para nosotros va muy lento. Es la naturaleza de nuestro propio deporte. Efectivamente lo que tenemos que conseguir es que entre corredores y equipos cada vez seamos más atractivos y multiplique las audiencias. Eso es lo que nos va a dar más derechos para llegar a esa parte a la que llegan otros deportes. Los esfuerzos económicos es de los diferentes sponsors que tenemos y es lo que hay. Estamos en un momento donde crecen los presupuestos de los equipos y el capital tiene que ser a base de los esfuerzos de los sponsors. Necesitamos compartir ciertos derechos para hacerlo más equilibrado y que sea un poco menos previsible de lo que a veces puede parecer. Bien es verdad que ahora que estamos viendo a un super deportista, si tienes la suerte de tenerlo, disfrutas más de ello. En ello estamos y cada vez más cerca de conseguirlo, esperamos". Movistar, antes Reynolds, Banesto, Illes Balears y Caisse d'Epargne. 46 años con grandes grandes leyendas como Perico, Induráin, Valverde, Nairo, Enric Mas.... La pregunta era obligada: ¿quién ha influido más? Unzué nombró a varios, pero no quiso mojarse: "En estos casi 50 años os podéis imaginar con toda la evolución que ha habido. Desde aquellos primeros años, la primera gran referencia fueron Perico Delgado, Ángel Arroyo, fueron claves. Era casi casi un niño y todo lo que ellos supusieron para nosotros fue increíble. Yo adquirí una parte importante de mi aprendizaje de ellos. Luego tuvimos la suerte que en el equipo amateur la llegada de un Miguel Induráin que con su forma de ganar sobre todo, nos ha dado esa solera de gran tipo de lo más respetado en el mundo del deporte. Todos ellos junto a los Gorospe... han sido los que han ayudado a que los ciclos de patrocinio de Reynolds, Banesto, Islas Baleares, Caisse d'Epargne y estos años de Telefónica, que se sientan orgullosos. Como todos los ciclos de patrocinio, tienen su principio y su fin, pero he tenido la suerte de encontrar esas grandes empresas y sobre todo tener acceso a grandes corredores españoles que nos ha permitido un gran palmarés y asegurar la continuidad tantos años", se extendió. Unzué dio un momento clave en el que los directivos de las grandes empresas se convencen de invertir en ciclismo: "Cuando los grandes ejecutivos han venido en nuestro coche, ahí es donde ellos son conscientes de dónde quieren invertir su dinero. A todo el que sigue una etapa en el coche les permite descubrir el ciclismo, y ahí es la base donde tratamos que nuestros sponsors que su intención está perfectamente hecha". Como no podía ser de otra manera, la charla viró hacia la figura de Enric Mas: "Para Telefónica es su segunda Vuelta a España. Es verdad que estos últimos años ganar a estos tres o cuatro fenómenos tiene esa parte muy interesante pero también tiene su parte limitadora para esos equipos que no pueden disfrutar de ellos. Lo que ha supuesto para Enric, con un nivel de profesionalidad increíble, ha acariciado victorias, ha pasado por momentos muy duros, ha sido capaz de recuperarse, convivir y no perder nunca la esperanza. Ha conseguido por fin la recompensa. Estoy seguro de que vamos a seguir viendo un Enric Mas al nivel de esta Vuelta a España los próximos 2-3 años. De cara a nuestros sponsors nos da mucha tranquilidad", explicó. Y también puso en valor la apuesta de Movistar por el equipo femenino al hablar de Paula Blasi: "El interés surgió en el año 17, cuando nos propusieron poner en marcha la estructura femenina. Como todo el resto de nuestros sponsors estaban encantados. La propia presidente de la asociación de equipos cuando se enteró que Telefónica montaba equipo femenino nos dio las gracias porque consideraba que iba a ayudar a impulsar el deporte femenino. Nos sentimos orgullosos de haber contribuido a la evolución de nuestro deporte de la mujer. Hace 8 años era casi un grupo de cicloturistas. Sin embargo, aquello fue el comienzo de una gran oportunidad. Han hecho del ciclismo femenino algo más atractivo y el resultado lo estamos viendo. Hemos visto una Vuelta a España fantástica, con la consolidación de Paula Blasi. En cuanto a la marca Movistar, los sentimos orgullosos de haber contribuido a la evolución de nuestro deporte", articuló manager general de Movistar Team. Unzué no rehuyó la pregunta de las dudas que ha suscitado Movistar en parte de la afición durante estos últimos años: "Es verdad que la década del 11 hasta hoy, en el 18 fuimos por cuarta o quinta vez el mejor equipo del mundo, hubo una transformación con la llegada de Sky (actual Ineos). Empezó a llegar el dinero y eso hizo que esos equilibrios se fueran perdiendo. Había mucha gente que te encontrabas a la que no podías tener acceso, no podías fichar. No hemos seguir la línea de resultados a la que estábamos acostumbrados. Éramos un equipo de naturaleza de vueltas de una semana y de grandes vueltas. Perico y Arroyo nos pusieron en esa dirección. Hemos conseguido en estas 46 temporadas 16 ó 17 grandes y siempre hemos tratado de tener los españoles más atractivos. No siempre ha podido ser. Estos últimos años es más difícil para nosotros que se nos pueda ver como a los que llevan más tiempo en el ciclismo nos veían. No es porque hayamos perdido la ilusión, es que te tienes que adaptar a la calidad de tus corredores", explicó. Y volvió a referirse a la figura de Enric Mas y esa Vuelta ganada: "Super emocionante porque ya llevábamos desde el 19 con Carapaz en el Giro que no lo habíamos conseguido. Habíamos estado cerca, teníamos podios. Cada vez es más difícil ganar. La clase media ha crecido una barbaridad y están esos tres, cuatro o cinco corredores que son casi intocables y es muy difícil estando ellos, ganar. Además tienen compañeros buenísimos. En el deporte de resistencia es muy difícil que no gane el mejor. Y cuando no lo tienes... Muy feliz por verle feliz, sobre todo lo que él disfrutó. Y la afición española, que nunca nos abandonó, pero hemos visto que necesitaba de esta victoria para disfrutar con él". Por último, dejó claro que no hay "nada" sobre el posible fichaje de Roglic y dijo que en los próximos años Movistar contará con "algún corredor español" capaz de ganar grandes vueltas, aunque no quiso dar un nombre propio.

articles.title: Why 'Shark Tank' star Kevin O'Leary wouldn't bring Jensen Huang back as Nvidia CEO
articles.summary: Mr. Wonderful isn't on the team clamoring to bring Jensen Huang back as Nvidia's CEO.
articles.body:
'Shark Tank' star and veteran investor Kevin O'Leary isn't aligning himself with the prominent voices calling for Nvidia ( NVDA ) to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO — a growing crowd in the billionaire land that is Silicon Valley.

"No, no, no, that's not going to happen. That will not happen," O'Leary said on Sozzi Unleashed . "It probably will never happen, because over the next two years, the amount of scrutiny this company is going to go through during this administration's microscope on it for the whole Chinese issue, you have so many agencies launching investigations domestically and internationally. I mean, you've got Treasury and Commerce at loggerheads right now. There's just too much noise to make that move."

The man who founded Nvidia ( NVDA ) in 1993 and turned it into the most important company in the AI revolution was ousted as CEO a week ago, following a period of explosive revelations and mounting controversy.

According to the New York Times, Huang's reported relationship with a woman suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence has put Nvidia under incredible scrutiny.

The Times also reported that Huang had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, one of roughly 60 people reporting directly to him. Reuters reported last Thursday that Huang had another relationship with an Nvidia employee whose identity has not been disclosed.

Huang, who has been married to his wife Lori for more than 40 years, now faces a stunning reversal for a leader whose reputation has been built on relentless execution and near-legendary control of Nvidia.

Nvidia's board reportedly has no plans to bring Huang back as CEO.

Huang broke his silence on Tuesday ahead of Nvidia's earnings release later in the afternoon.

"Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO," Huang said in a statement .
