articles.title: SpaceX is leasing $47 billion of Nvidia chips like a car — and lenders hold the title
articles.summary: Leasing a car gets you the newest model for a monthly payment, and the bank keeps the title. SpaceX just signed the AI version on about $47 billion of Nvidia...
articles.body:
Leasing a car gets you the newest model for a monthly payment, and the bank keeps the title. SpaceX ( SPCX ) just signed the AI version on about $47 billion of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) newest chips.

Goldman Sachs ( GS ) and Apollo Global Management ( APO ) could start selling pieces of the roughly $40 billion deal as soon as this week, Bloomberg reported Tuesday. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)

An Apollo-backed vehicle buys Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Vera Rubin chips and rents them to SpaceX ( SPCX ), keeping the debt off its books . Goldman leads an $8.3 billion senior secured loan , which gets repaid first and is backed by the chips.

Wall Street has spent six weeks dumping the AI trade . Now it's being asked to bankroll the biggest chip bill yet, just as the Bank of Nvidia pulls back .

The fine print reads like any car lease, with more zeros. SpaceX put $7 billion down, and each batch of chips is leased for about five years, running into 2032. Rent is owed even if the chips are damaged. No early returns.

SpaceX doesn't guarantee what the chips are worth at the end. Lenders take that risk, and Nvidia plans two newer chips by 2028. In AI years, a five-year-old chip is a clunker.

SpaceX's own debt climbed to nearly $39 billion by Sept. 30 from about $23 billion at the end of 2025. Its five-year credit default swaps , which insure against a default, rose from about 110 basis points at the June IPO to around 265 on Nov. 16. That implies roughly 20% odds of default within five years, by Yahoo Finance calculations.

SpaceX finance chief Bret Johnsen cited "less than one year payback periods" on AI infrastructure. But the rent runs five years. And one customer, identified by Bloomberg as Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ), supplied about a third of SpaceX's third quarter revenue on a contract that can end with 90 days' notice. If that business walks, the rent doesn't.

SpaceX's lease tops everything CoreWeave ( CRWV ) has borrowed against its chips since 2023. Goldman's credit team expects AI chip financing to grow almost sevenfold next year .

"Financing is becoming one of these bottlenecks, right? Because there are only so many dollars out there for these companies and they need it," Siebert Financial chief investment officer Mark Malek told Yahoo Finance .

Wall Street is stepping in as Nvidia steps back

Nvidia's off-balance-sheet commitments doubled in a quarter to $422 billion , according to JPMorgan's Michael Cembalest. Dan Niles of Niles Investment Management told Deirdre Bosa Live the Bank of Nvidia is "going to be closed for a bit."

articles.title: Apple reports outages after an internal update, says it is working to get systems back online
articles.summary: Apple said it was experiencing tech issues Tuesday that were affecting several of its popular consumer-facing services.
articles.body: Apple said it was experiencing tech issues Tuesday that were affecting several of its popular consumer-facing services. As of 2 p.m. ET, Apple’s own system status page showed that Apple Business, Apple School Manager, AppleCare, iCloud Mail and Web Apps, and SchoolWork were each experiencing outages. Earlier, the page showed the App Store and Apple Music experiencied outages. “Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning,” an Apple spokesperson told NBC News. “We’re working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible.” At Apple stores in New York and Chicago, employees told NBC News earlier in the day that their internal software had stopped working and they had been unable to complete purchases or make appointments. Over the past week, U.S. residents have experienced a cascade of technical issues that have led to nationwide outages of key consumer services, including email, air travel and online banking. While none of the issues appear to be related, they’ve exposed America’s reliance on older infrastructure and revealed the extent to which companies and governments are being forced to upgrade systems in the AI age. The incidents have also stoked unfounded paranoia that something larger may be afoot.

articles.title: China, Canada expand tariff relief after Carney-Xi meeting
articles.summary: China offers tariff cuts on Canadian pork and seafood, as Canada extends exemptions for Chinese steel and aluminium.
articles.body:
Canada and China have agreed to cut tariffs on more goods, as Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney continues to look to decrease his country’s dependence on the United States amid President Donald Trump’s tariffs.

Meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on Tuesday, Carney and Chinese President Xi Jinping announced new tariff remissions, building on an agreement they made in January to open up trade and start to repair a strained diplomatic relationship.

China will offer tariff relief on about 400 million Canadian dollars ($280m) worth of Canadian exports, including frozen pork and seafood, said a statement from Carney’s office.

Canada, in exchange, will keep tariff exemptions for certain Chinese steel and aluminium products in place for another two years, and add remissions to another 32 steel and aluminium items that Canada doesn’t have enough of.

Xi said stronger ties served both countries’ interests and supported global stability and prosperity.

Carney praised the greater predictability in the relationship and said Canada was ahead of schedule on its goal of increasing exports to China by 50 percent by the end of the decade.

Under the January agreement, Canada lowered its 100 percent tariff on Chinese electric vehicles to 6.1 percent, allowing an initial 49,000 vehicles into the country each year. That cap is set to rise to 70,000 over five years.

In return, China agreed to lower tariffs on Canadian agricultural products and recently extended relief for canola meal, peas, lobster and crab for another two years.

The deal comes a day after Carney said Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if talks with Washington fail to hold together the closely integrated North American auto industry.

“We have the best auto workers in the world, and we want them fully deployed, full opportunity, in an integrated North American market,” Carney told reporters in Cambodia on Monday. “That market has become less integrated because of US trade actions.”

The comments prompted a backlash from White House trade adviser Peter Navarro, who responded by asking whether Carney was threatening to “play China off the US”.

“This is offensive in the extreme,” he said, adding that Carney should be more worried that China would “eat Canada alive”.

Carney has made looking to markets beyond the US a central part of his economic strategy, as Trump’s tariffs hit Canadian industries, including auto manufacturing, as well as steel and aluminium.

Trade talks between Ottawa and Washington broke down in August , but Carney said on Saturday that he’d spoken with Trump and senior officials, and that while differences remained, there was progress towards a possible deal.

He also met with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum on Tuesday, with both countries reaffirming their commitment to renew the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement , according to Carney’s office.

One year after Carney visited Mexico, during which they launched a strategic partnership, the two leaders agreed to keep expanding bilateral trade and investment. They also highlighted a 19-percent increase in merchandise trade in the first nine months of this year, compared with the same period last year.

images.caption: Delegations led by Chinese President Xi Jinping and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney attend a bilateral meeting ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China’s Guangdong province [Maxim Shemetov/Pool via AFP]

articles.title: Anthropic IPO: How to buy a company's stock when it IPOs
articles.summary: Learn how to buy Anthropic stock when it IPOs on Nasdaq Nov. 19: Request shares at the offer price through your broker or buy it on the open market.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

AI company Anthropic is set to start trading under ticker "ANT" on Thursday, Nov. 19, after the offer price is finalized on the evening of Nov. 18. The offering covers 825 million Class A shares with pricing expected to be between $70 and $78 per share.

Here's what you need to know about buying Anthropic shares at the offer price or once it launches on the Nasdaq.

The table below highlights key points on the Anthropic IPO, including the ticker, expected per-share pricing, and estimated valuation range.

You have two options for buying an IPO stock. You can access shares from your broker at the offer price if you're eligible, or you can purchase shares on the open market.

1. From your broker, if you are eligible

IPO underwriters allocate shares to institutional investors and retail brokers like Fidelity and Schwab. The brokers, in turn, offer those shares to their account holders. Because the share supply is finite, brokers typically limit access to account holders who meet certain eligibility requirements.

Each broker sets its own eligibility requirements and rules for allocating its block of shares. To participate, you generally have to request access by submitting a conditional offer or indication of interest with your broker. Allocations are not guaranteed.

The underwriters and the company going public set the final IPO price just before trading begins. If your broker fulfills your conditional offer, it will be at the IPO price, but the number of shares may be less than what you requested.

2. On the open market, after trading starts

If you didn't request IPO access from your broker, weren't eligible to participate, or weren't allocated shares, you can buy the stock in your brokerage account once trading begins. The price will be driven by market forces and may be higher or lower than the IPO price.

Brokers sell IPO shares at the offer price, also called the IPO price or offering price. The exact process varies by broker, but usually involves these steps:

Review upcoming offerings. Your broker may list upcoming IPOs on a webpage, or share them via email alerts.

Read the prospectus. The prospectus describes the company's business model, financial history, and risk factors. Your broker may ask you to certify that you've read it as part of your conditional offer submission.

Check eligibility requirements. Brokers use different methods to distribute limited IPO shares among their customer bases. Some enforce minimum account balance requirements, and others, including Robinhood, may use random or proportional allocation systems. There are also FINRA rules that prohibit certain people close to the transaction, called "restricted persons," from participating. FINRA is a regulatory body that oversees brokerage firms and their trading activity.

Learn the rules. Your broker may not allow margin buying and likely imposes penalties for selling IPO shares too quickly. For example, Robinhood can restrict your access to future IPOs for 60 days if you sell IPO shares within 30 days.

Submit a conditional offer to purchase or indication of interest. Your conditional offer specifies how many shares you want to buy. You generally won't know the offer price at this time. Your broker may require you to complete an eligibility questionnaire and certification as part of the conditional offer.

Affirm the offer. The broker will share the IPO price when it's available. Some brokers ask you to affirm the price and number of shares. Others may only require the affirmation if the price changed significantly from the initial estimate.

You may not receive the full number of shares requested, or any at all. Your broker should confirm your final allocated share count the morning that public trading begins, or sooner.

You can buy a stock after it IPOs by placing a trade with your broker. At that point, the per-share price will be dictated by supply and demand. It can remain close to the offer price or diverge significantly. A look at four recent technology IPOs, shown in the table below, demonstrates this range.

Highly anticipated IPOs like Anthropic often perform well in their first trading days.

IPO stocks can reprice quickly, so many investors use limit orders to manage their price exposure. A limit order to buy a stock defines the maximum price you will pay. If you want to hold your financial investment in Anthropic at $90 per share, you would specify that in a limit order. A full or partial trade will only happen if shares are available at that price.

A market order to buy a stock executes the trade at the best available price. This can be risky when prices are changing quickly. You might decide to request the trade when the stock is at $90, but it could jump to $100 or more before your order is executed. A market order will be executed regardless, assuming you have sufficient cash to cover it.

There's a chance you won't get any shares. You may not be eligible through your broker, for example, and your limit order may not be fulfilled — particularly if you are conservative about the price. In that case, you have two options: Wait for the price to fall or invest in indirect exposure.

Waiting out early volatility (and lock-up expiration)

IPOs can spike in their early days and then level out in the weeks and months that follow. This pattern can be shaped by limited share supply. Brokers discourage retail investors from selling their IPO shares quickly, and underwriters often prohibit company insiders from liquidating.

The insider restrictions are defined in what's called a lock-up agreement. A simple lock-up might ban insiders from selling their shares for 90 days from the IPO date. If insiders start selling after 90 days, the share supply expands, and the share price may soften.

Anthropic has a tiered lock-up schedule that allows insider shares to be sold in batches. Non-founding directors, officers, and certain employees can sell up to 10% of their shares right away, while co-founders and certain shareholders owning more than 0.5% of the company have more rigid requirements. They can sell some of their shares earlier but remain restricted from liquidating for a year or until after the release of Anthropic's third quarter 2027 earnings, whichever is earlier.

About 15.5 billion shares are locked up for up to 180 days. Co-founders and holders above 0.5% of fully diluted shares are locked up for up to 365 days.

Non-founder directors, officers, and employees can sell up to 10% starting the first trading day.

If the stock price continues to trade above your pricing comfort zone, you can research indirect ownership opportunities. This involves buying a fund or a company that owns the IPO stock you want.

Funds that already have pre-IPO Anthropic exposure include:

Public venture fund VCX by Fundrise ( VCX )

Once Anthropic begins trading, it will likely appear in other funds, including index ETFs. Large IPOs are eligible for the Nasdaq-100 after 15 trading days, which means Anthropic could be added to funds tracking that index within weeks.

Invesco QQQ ( QQQ ) and State Street SPDR Portfolio Nasdaq-100 ETF ( QNDX ) are two options. Other funds to watch include iShares Russell 1000 Growth ETF ( IWF ) and First Trust U.S. Equity Opportunities ETF ( FPX ).

These public companies will have Anthropic exposure after the IPO:

Amazon and Alphabet, the parent company of Google, are the largest reported outside investors.

Volatility is the headlining risk of IPO investing. Per-share prices can rise quickly in the early days and then decline once the hype dies down. Investors willing to buy shares at any price can be stuck in a loss position for an extended time.

This has been the story for some shareholders of Cerebras, the AI infrastructure company that went public in May of 2026. Cerebras closed its first day of trading at $311.07 and was down to about $100 six months later.

That isn't always the trajectory for IPOs, but it happens often enough to be wary of the risk. Reasons why newly public companies are prone to price volatility include:

Headlines and excitement can encourage investors to spend more per share than the business warrants, and those who paid high prices can be quick to sell if growth doesn't materialize.

Newly public companies have limited operating history to evaluate, sometimes involving very fast revenue growth, so establishing a reasonable buy-price threshold is difficult.

Expiring lock-up agreements can increase the supply of public shares rapidly, putting downward pressure on the stock price.

Investor and regulatory scrutiny adds pressure to the management team, which can distract from business execution.

IPO companies may not be profitable . Anthropic had an operating loss of nearly $1.3 billion in the first nine months of 2026, down from $5.2 billion in the prior-year period. According to Anthropic's S-1 , the combination of the company's revenue growth, compute efficiency, and operating efficiency has resulted in an adjusted operating margin of 15% and adjusted operating income of $2.5 billion for the three months ended Sept. 30, 2026, compared to an adjusted operating margin of negative 93% and adjusted operating loss of $1.3 billion for the three months ended Sept. 30, 2025.

IPO investment opportunities typically aren't go-or-no-go choices. Rather than deciding whether you should buy Anthropic stock, consider the pricing and portfolio allocation that make the investment worthwhile. That requires a detailed read of the company's S-1 and a review of your investment time horizon and risk tolerance.

A conservative buy price and a small share count keep your risk low, while a larger order can increase your opportunity for gains.

You can buy Anthropic stock within a brokerage account starting on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026.

The Anthropic IPO price is expected to be $70 to $78 per share, and will be finalized the evening of Nov. 18, 2026.

Can non-US investors buy Anthropic stock?

The Anthropic IPO will include offerings to several countries outside the U.S., including Australia, Canada, Japan, Switzerland, and the UK. Non-U.S. investors can check with their brokers to see if they have access and how to request shares. Anthropic does not currently plan to list its shares for public trading on foreign exchanges.

Your broker determines whether you have access to IPOs in your IRA. For example, Robinhood provides IPO access within its standard brokerage accounts, but retirement accounts, multiple individual investing accounts, joint accounts, custodial, and managed accounts aren't eligible for IPO access.

There is no restriction on buying the stock in an IRA once it begins trading publicly. The difference is that you'll pay the market price rather than the IPO price.

The IPO price is a set price for the initial sale of shares before the stock begins trading on the open market. Anthropic will set its IPO price on Nov. 18, based on demand. This per-share price establishes Anthropic's opening valuation, which typically changes quickly once the shares are freely traded.

articles.title: Kalshi halts Trump speech bets after CFTC order
articles.summary: Kalshi halts Trump speech bets following CFTC mandate amid concerns of insider trading in US prediction markets.
articles.body:
The prediction market platform Kalshi has ended wagers on whether United States President Donald Trump would use specific words on certain dates in his speeches.

The decision, revealed on Tuesday, comes amid an order from the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the federal agency that oversees futures trading, which last week called on the company to end the bets.

Earlier this year, Kalshi’s surveillance system flagged to the agency potential insider trading concerns involving these markets. It was later discovered that a White House teleprompter operator had traded on markets related to the president’s comments.

The teleprompter operator, Gabriel Perez, received a three-year ban from the platform and was required to pay $65,000 in penalties, as well as relinquish his $107,000 in winnings to the CFTC. By August, the CFTC had begun an internal review of prediction markets, according to CNBC.

The move comes amid a new wave of scrutiny of prediction market platforms by the CFTC. That marks a shift from the stance of Chair Michael Selig, who had previously championed the emerging industry, but has now adopted a tougher tone, launching investigations into Kalshi and its competitor Polymarket, which is not regulated by the commission.

Kalshi, in particular, had been under investigation for developing new products without notifying the commission, according to a report by Politico earlier this month.

The development also comes as Donald Trump Jr, the president’s eldest son, stepped down from his role as a paid strategic adviser to the company last week.

While Kalshi has pulled markets involving mentions by the president, wagers on what other prominent figures will say remain active.

These include predictions about comments by elected US officials, including Vice President JD Vance and New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, at the upcoming New York Times DealBook Summit, as well as remarks by executives at Microsoft and SpaceX. Other active markets concern what companies such as Nvidia and retail giant Target will say during their earnings calls.

Kalshi has also stopped listing some markets at the request of the regulatory agency, including certain sports-related markets, according to the Reuters news agency.

Neither Kalshi nor the CFTC responded to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

articles.title: Microsoft's AI pitch at Ignite: Cheaper models as business 'token spend is going through the roof'
articles.summary: Microsoft rolled out new features to its AI initiative and products during its flagship conference on Tuesday. One theme was keeping enterprise costs down.
articles.body:
Microsoft ( MSFT ) announced a slew of AI improvements at its Ignite conference on Tuesday. One message stood out: The tech giant is focused on making AI cheaper for businesses by offering specialized models for specific tasks. In some cases, the tasks that would've taken the company weeks were performed in minutes.

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman said he is hearing time and again from enterprises that "token spend is going through the roof."

"Our commitment is to give you the very best price performance out there, so that you can really scale your agents," Suleyman said. "And we also know that you want models that feel truly yours."

During the conference, executives highlighted Microsoft IQ, a new platform designed to help businesses organize and share employees' knowledge, expertise, and tools. The idea is to help AI systems learn how a company works and build on that knowledge over time.

CEO Satya Nadella highlighted the launch of new AI models for coding, cybersecurity, and decision making. The company's flagship coding model, MAI Code 2, is designed to handle complex, time-consuming programming tasks, work across multiple files, and understand entire software projects.

Nadella also underscored Copilot Fusion, which orchestrates "multiple models to deliver frontier-level results at significantly lower costs."

Microsoft highlighted a feature that selects the right model for the task, making it easier to maximize output quality while managing the cost of each request.

Nadella kicked off the conference by acknowledging last week's outage, which spanned regions.

"We know the trust you place in our services and take that responsibility very seriously, and in that context, I know we have work to do," Nadella said.

"We are committed to ensuring that we learn and we continuously improve," he added.

articles.body:
The FBI said on Monday that the Chase outage was connected to a software release, not malicious activity.

The agency told The Hill’s sister network NewsNation that it didn’t see any signs pointing toward malicious or external activity in the outage, finding that it was linked to a software release.

In a Monday post to the social platform X , Chase said that it “has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems – there is no evidence this is cyber-related.”

“It is taking longer than usual to service some customers. Where we were party to a transaction involving other banks, those banks may have been impacted, but this is not a systemic issue,” the bank continued.

Customers at Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank and Truist on Monday reported problems accessing their accounts — an issue that followed two outage incidents with Microsoft Outlook and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

Downdetector, an outage tracker website, reported that Chase, Bank of America, U.S. Bank and Wells Fargo customers were the most impacted by the outages.

Fifty-two percent of the reports from Chase customers struggled with account balances and transactions, 21 percent experienced trouble with web logins and another 17 percent dealt with transfer and wire issues.

When customers tried to get into the Chase mobile app, they were met with messages that said, “Some services aren’t available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.”

articles.title: Nvidia board rules out Jensen Huang’s return as CEO
articles.summary: Nvidia’s board unanimously accepted former CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation, and does not intend to reinstate him as chief executive, board chair Harvey Jones said at the start of the company’s earnings call Tuesday night.
articles.body: Nvidia’s board unanimously accepted former CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation, and does not intend to reinstate him as chief executive, board chair Harvey Jones said at the start of the company’s earnings call Tuesday night. The announcement comes after Huang said in a statement earlier Tuesday that he would be “honored” to return as CEO, despite his resignation amid national security concerns and reports of multiple extramarital affairs. Jones said Nvidia’s board has “every confidence” in CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress to lead the company as it searches for a permanent leader. The company sought to reassure investors and offer clarity about its future in the third-quarter earnings report Tuesday evening, with Kress, saying Nvidia’s “roadmap is on track, and our ambition has never been greater.” “Our ambition will not change, our passion to innovate will not change, and our commitment to customers, partners, and shareholders will not change,” Kress told investors, whose confidence in the company’s future has been badly shaken by the scandal, on the earnings call. It’s the first financial picture investors are getting since the chipmaker was shaken last week by Huang’s resignation after three decades at the helm of the company he founded. Nvidia more than doubled its quarterly revenue and profit from a year prior, and both figures beat Wall Street’s expectations. Nvidia’s earnings — the numbers and executives’ comments — have long been viewed as a bellwether for the larger AI industry, with Nvidia’s technology and funding at the heart of much of the boom. That’s especially true now with questions swirling about the industry’s future without Huang, its biggest cheerleader and dealmaker, at the helm. Nvidia shares were coming off their worst week in 19 months heading into the report. The stock is down 16.7% since Huang admitted to an extramarital affair and Nvidia’s board launched an investigation into whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, erasing $751 billion in market value. Since Nvidia shares hit their record high on October 6, they have dropped 35%, erasing roughly $2 trillion in market value. Ahead of the report, Siebert Financial Chief Investment Officer Mark Malek wrote that it would be the “most important in the company’s history.” Nvidia shares have dropped for four consecutive days since Huang resigned. Shares fell just 0.44% Tuesday. But shares moved higher in after-hours trading after the earnings release, gaining roughly 2%. “The massive results, strong guidance and reassurance that the strategy Huang put in place remains firmly on track show that an orderly CEO transition does not necessarily have to dilute the company’s value,” Thomas Monteiro, senior analyst at Investing.com, said in emailed commentary following the release. He added that Nvidia’s growth train “can continue with or without Huang, provided the company makes the right call on leadership.” Nvidia’s board said last week that Kress, the company’s CFO of 13 years, would serve as interim CEO as it considered internal and external candidates to permanently fill the role. Nvidia’s board also said Tuesday it had established a new national security and export control oversight committee to ensure the company is abiding by global trade regulations, and that it will strengthen its internal national security and compliance initiatives. Some Nvidia employees, investors and other tech leaders had called on the board to reinstate Huang as CEO, pending the outcome of its investigation into his multiple reported extramarital affairs, including with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom US officials suspect as a potential Chinese intelligence asset; and at least one direct subordinate at Nvidia. Huang said Tuesday that he would be “honored” to return as CEO if the board decided that his “return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America,” in his first public comment since resigning. Jones said during Tuesday’s call that he would not take additional questions regarding Huang’s resignation or the company’s investigation, but that the board would “communicate further when appropriate.” Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president and general manager of Hyperscale and High-Performance Computing, joined Kress to take analyst questions on the call — a signal of his importance as a senior leader at the company. Meanwhile, Huang is set to testify on Capitol Hill on December 1. He is expected to face questions about his relationship with Alice Huang and Nvidia’s sales of chips to Singapore-based Megaspeed, which some US officials believed should have been labeled a national security risk. Some US sources say that whether or not Alice Huang was recruited by China’s intelligence service, she posed a counterintelligence risk because Chinese national security law requires its citizens to assist in intelligence-gathering efforts if asked. Concerns have been mounting that chips Megaspeed purchased were diverted to Chinese entities, potentially skirting US export restrictions. Another strong quarter Huang’s exit aside, concerns about whether the AI trade is a bubble about to burst, with valuations and infrastructure spending outpacing returns, had already begun to reach a fever pitch in recent months. Gary Gensler, the former top cop on Wall Street, told CNN this week that he believes the AI bubble will likely burst and cause a recession prior to the 2028 presidential election. Nvidia’s Tuesday report indicates that, at least for now, the company’s growth continues to outpace Wall Street’s expectations. The company posted $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, up 103% year-on-year. Profits reached more than $65 billion, up 105% year-on-year. Kress also said demand for the company’s next-generation Vera Rubin AI computing technology is “off to an explosive start,” with the tech already in use by customers such as Google, Microsoft and Oracle. Demand for Nvidia’s chips remains strong, with a handful of the biggest AI and cloud companies expected to shell out more than $1 trillion in capital expenditures next year alone. But in the wake of Huang’s exit, investors have been more concerned with the company’s future business. The report also comes after a blue wave in the US midterm elections ushered in a slate of newly elected leaders, many of whom campaigned on slowing or restricting data center development, which could dent Nvidia’s business. Analysts with research firm IDC wrote in a report last week that the firm sees “near-term AI infrastructure demand and supply as largely locked in, so the harder questions,” like long-term bets on emerging technologies and the financing system that Jensen Huang sat in the center of, “sit further out.” Nvidia said it expects fourth quarter revenue to come in around $130 billion, plus or minus 3% — exceeding what Wall Street analysts had predicted, according to consensus estimates from FactSet. Significant questions also remain about the future of Nvidia’s business in China, and potentially in Asia more broadly, as US officials react to the national security concerns surrounding the company. Shipments of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China made up less than 1% of sales in its core data center business in the previous quarter. However, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & co, estimated that China and Hong Kong “could comprise roughly 15% of revenues when considering potential loopholes throughout Asia.” The Commerce Department on Monday tightened export restrictions designed to prevent China from accessing sensitive, AI-powering computer chips via data centers in third-party countries. The company earned $2.4 billion in sales of licensed chips to China during the third quarter, but it has ceased such shipments, Kress said during Tuesday’s call. This story has been updated with additional details and context.

articles.title: Democratic lawmakers slam Huang statement on possible Nvidia return: ‘Slow your roll’
articles.summary: Top Democrats criticized ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s statement that he was willing to return to the company he co-founded, as Huang prepares to answer questions before Congress on his extramarital affairs and possible national security risks. Huang resigned as CEO of the tech giant following revelations that he had a relationship with a woman the…
articles.body:
Top Democrats criticized ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s statement that he was willing to return to the company he co-founded, as Huang prepares to answer questions before Congress on his extramarital affairs and possible national security risks.

Huang resigned as CEO of the tech giant following revelations that he had a relationship with a woman the U.S. government suspected was a spy for China, named Alice Huang, but suggested on Tuesday that he is open to returning as the chief executive.

“I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation,” Huang wrote on the social platform X. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

President Trump suggested he would be open to Huang’s return, but top Democrats are now saying not so fast.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries told The Atlantic on Tuesday, “you’ve got to be kidding me right now.”

Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.) replied to Huang’s post on X, saying “slow your roll there.”

“You have to answer some questions first,” Gallego wrote . “Did you know that Megaspeed was under investigation in 2024 and if so why did you allow the sales to go forward?”

Megaspeed is a Singaporean data center company where Alice Huang was once an executive, and which the U.S. is currently investigating .

Huang is set to testify before three congressional committees at the request of House Republicans — the foreign affairs, China and intelligence committees — on Dec. 1.

“The American people need answers on Mr. Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous PRC actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal,” the committee chairs said in a statement.

House Democrats are concerned not only with Huang’s actions but also with his relationship to Trump . The pair have worked closely together since Trump returned to office.

The New York Times reported that the president was briefed twice on Huang’s relationship with a suspected spy, but did not appear to take any action, and later allowed Nvidia to sell its high-powered chips to China.

With Democrats gaining sizable majorities in both chambers next year, they will have the authority to pursue investigations into Nvidia, Huang and other Trump allies.

Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.), the likely next chair of the foreign affairs committee, suggested that there would be more to come even before Huang said he could return to Nvidia.

“We’ve seen the tip of the iceberg,” Meeks told reporters last week. “The board probably did what it had to do. I have other questions. This doesn’t make it go away.”

articles.title: Have you been able to find a seasonal job?
articles.summary: The hiring season for holiday jobs is already well underway, and the early reads on this year’s hiring activity seem fairly positive.
articles.body: The hiring season for holiday jobs is already well underway, and the early reads on this year’s hiring activity seem fairly positive. As of September, seasonal job postings were running about 10% ahead of last year and 7% above 2019 levels, according to Indeed. Through October, seasonal hiring announcements were up 26% from last year’s record-low levels, according to Challenger, Gray & Christmas, an outplacement and business research firm that’s been tracking seasonal hiring plans since 2012. But as the labor market evolves, these temporary but crucial roles (and who’s filling them) may look a bit different than they have in the past. That’s because the seasonal announcements Challenger is tracking are concentrated among fewer employers. And the seasonal job postings from Indeed are broadening beyond sales floors and into warehouses and vehicles. In the backdrop, this is a “low-hire, low-fire” environment that has left few opportunities for full-time employment – it’s taking job seekers an average of six months to find work. If you’ve been on the job hunt for a seasonal role; if you’ve successfully landed one; or if you’re looking to hire seasonal workers, we’d like to interview you for an upcoming article. We want to hear about your experiences, the reasons why you’ve been looking for a holiday job, and what you’ve been able to find.

articles.title: US Fed’s Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House hearing
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has been trying to fire Cook since August 2025.
articles.body:
United States Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook has declined, through her lawyers, to appear next month before a Trump administration committee that is considering whether she should be fired, calling the process unfair and committed to a predetermined outcome.

The refusal extends the wrangling between the White House and Cook’s lawyers regarding her appearance before the committee, which the administration of US President Donald Trump initially demanded for November 6.

Administration officials have called on Cook to appear before the committee to address allegations that she committed mortgage fraud in 2021, before she joined the Fed’s board of governors, a charge she denies. Cook has not been charged with any crime.

Trump has sought to fire Cook since August 2025, and she has argued that the president’s efforts to do so represent a threat to the Fed’s independence and reflect Trump’s desire to force the central bank to reduce borrowing costs.

“Governor Cook has no legal obligation to participate in an unfair hearing — and indeed, has a duty to the Federal Reserve to decline to participate in any proceeding that would undermine the institution’s unique status and independence,” Abbe David Lowell, Cook’s lawyer, wrote in a letter released on Tuesday to White House counsel William Scharf. The three-person panel set up by the White House to consider the allegations “appears to be a facade designed to obscure a predetermined decision to fire Governor Cook”, the letter said.

In June, the US Supreme Court blocked Trump from removing Cook while litigation over the attempted firing continues, finding that “the fact of independence but also the appearance of independence is key to the Federal Reserve’s design”.

Trump officials have threatened to move ahead with the hearing even without Cook, and in a November 3 letter said that the three-member committee “reserves the right to draw adverse inferences against you” for not participating.

The unusual “committee of inquiry” set up by the White House consists of Kevin Hassett, Trump’s top economic adviser; Andrea Lucas, whom Trump appointed to lead the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission; and Keith Sonderling, Trump’s pick for Department of Labor secretary.

The Supreme Court said in a footnote to its June ruling that Trump could try again to fire Cook if the administration provided her adequate notice and an opportunity to respond. The committee of inquiry is an effort to meet those conditions.

Under the law governing the Fed, the president can only fire a Fed governor “for cause”, but the Supreme Court didn’t address whether Cook’s actions met that standard. The committee will ultimately recommend whether there is cause to fire Cook, the White House has said.

articles.title: AMD, Broadcom, CoreWeave stocks rise on Nvidia earnings beat
articles.summary: Semiconductor and AI infrastructure stocks moved higher in after-hours trading on Tuesday after AI chip heavyweight Nvidia posted better-than-expected quarte...
articles.body:
Semiconductor and neocloud provider stocks rose on Tuesday in after-hours trading as AI chip-heavy Nvidia ( NVDA ) reported Q3 results that beat Wall Street's expectations. Peers AMD ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) shares rose more than 1% in post-market trading. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company ( TSM ), which manufactures Nvidia's chips, also saw its stock rise 2%.

The semiconductor trade has been volatile since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO last Thursday following reports of extramarital affairs. Wall Street's questions over a succession plan have kept shares of the AI chip heavyweight and the AI trade under pressure.

"I hope that this helps to calm some jitters in the market about the transition," Brian Colello, Morningstar analyst, told Deirdre Bosa Live on Tuesday.

"Seems like business as usual and the forecast is really encouraging as well," he added.

The analyst said there are still plenty more questions but that Nvidia reiterating its long-term financial forecast is helpful to the market.

Other areas of the chip trade also rose, including memory chipmaker Micron Technology ( MU ) and SK Hynix ( SKHY ), which rose modestly.

Meanwhile, Nvidia-backed CoreWeave ( CRWV ) popped 2%. Nvidia ( NVDA ) owns more than 10% of CoreWeave and is a major chip supplier to the AI infrastructure provider. Peer Nebius ( NBIS ) also rose 3%.

articles.title: Contest adverse HC orders on pensions, says EPFO
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: EPFO has asked its officers to aggressively contest adverse HC rulings in pension on higher wages (PoHW) cases under Employees' Pension Scheme
articles.body: NEW DELHI: EPFO has asked its officers to aggressively contest adverse HC rulings in pension on higher wages (PoHW) cases under Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS), as the judgements have largely favoured pensioners and struck down the retirement savings body's circulars.To fight legal challenges arising from court rulings, field offices have been given standard defence templates and told to cite SC's Nov 2022 judgement in the Sunil Kumar case to secure division-bench stays against adverse single-judge orders and seek swift disposal, TOI has learnt. Central Board of Trustee is expected to discuss the matter Thursday.Under EPS, employee pension contributions and payouts were historically linked to the statutory wage cap regardless of actual earnings. At a monthly cap of Rs 15,000, 8.33% went towards EPS even if an employee earned Rs 1 lakh a month.Para 11(3) originally allowed employers and employees to jointly opt for contributions on actual salaries to secure a proportionately higher monthly pension. Govt deleted this provision in Aug 2014.In Nov 2022, SC upheld the 2014 amendments but gave eligible members in service on Sept 1, 2014, four months to apply for higher pensions. It excluded pre-2014 retirees who had missed the option.Nearly 99% of PoHW applications have been processed and settled, but about 2,800 cases remain in HCs. In many cases, EPFO remains in contempt for not complying with rulings. The disputes fall into several categories.Although SC's 2022 ruling barred pre-2014 retirees who missed para 11(3) option from opting for PoHW, Kerala and Punjab & Haryana HCs granted relief. They ruled that a 2016 order continued to protect them and allowed people retiring after Sept 2014 to exercise the option.Another group of cases concerns exempted PF trusts, which manage employee funds under EPFO norms. Mostly public sector companies such as BHEL and NLC had capped contributions, but employees sought higher pensions after SC ruling. EPFO rejected the demand, but Madras and Calcutta HCs set aside its decision. In Sept, EPFO secured a stay on contempt proceedings.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Read everything that Nvidia’s board chair had to say about Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia’s first board chair, Harvey C. Jones,  led the company’s first earnings call since Jensen Huang’s resignation.
articles.body: Nvidia’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday was its first with CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress at the helm alongside the company’s first board chair, Harvey C. Jones. The leadership change followed Jensen Huang’s resignation last week after reports he had multiple affairs – including one with former Megaspeed executive and alleged Chinese asset Alice Huang and one with a direct report, Kimberly Powell. Nvidia is investigating whether Huang’s relationship with the former compromised national security or company secrets. Huang will also testify before lawmakers on December 1st. Ahead of Tuesday’s earnings, Huang said he would be willing to return as CEO. However, during the company’s earnings call, Jones stated that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted [Huang’s] resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” Jones also said that during the call, the company would not be addressing or taking questions “regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation.” He added that, “the Board is proactively dealing with the immediate consequences facing the company, as well as enhancing our oversight capacity going forward.” In Tuesday’s earnings Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, continuing years of skyrocketing revenue driven by the AI industry. Jones shared the following update on the company: > As Chairman of NVIDIA’s Board of Directors, I want to say a few words on the Board’s behalf. NVIDIA is an exceptionally strong company. Its strength comes from its extraordinary people, groundbreaking technology, and exemplary track record of execution. Our financial performance speaks for itself. > On November 12th, our Board of Directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as President, CEO, and board member. The NVIDIA Board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO. The Board appointed Colette Kress, NVIDIA’s longtime and well-respected CFO, as interim CEO. In addition, the Board announced it was initiating a search for a permanent chief executive, and we have since retained Heidrick and Struggles to lead the search. > While this was an unexpected transition, the Board acted deliberately and in the best interest of the company’s employees, customers, partners, and shareholders. This morning, the company announced that our Board has established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee that will include a select group of our independent Board directors, senior external advisors, and legal counsel. > This committee will enhance— will– excuse me, will enhance our engagement with the U.S. government, including all relevant agencies. We will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation. Our Board will communicate further when appropriate. On behalf of our shareholders, the Board is proactively dealing with the immediate consequences facing the company, as well as enhancing our oversight capacity going forward. > We have an incredibly talented leadership team, and we have every confidence in Colette’s leadership, integrity, and ability to deliver as interim CEO. Colette has been at the center of this company’s extraordinary growth for the last— growth for the last 13 years, instrumental in executing strategy, and with a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations, and financial position. The Board and the entire leadership team remain laser-focused on driving NVIDIA forward. Our commitment to generating value for shareholders, customers, and partners remains unchanged.
